selected.positive: Existing LFM3-1.7B-Base is a pretraining artifact, not this 2026-10 1.73B full post-trained agent model. SFT+mixed RL+multi-domain distillation+agentic RL yields browser and tool-task abilities unavailable in the Base. Publisher WebArena-Verified 38.42%, Qwen3.5-9B 28.94% in reported table, 1.7B agent specialization worth preserving.
selected.negative: Publisher benchmark not independent, evaluates specific agent scaffold, may not generalize to coding. Same card GPQA 63.37% versus Qwen3.5-9B 80.40%, RULER128K 65.56 vs 87.11. Not superhuman general intelligence; risk of losing agent-finetuned weights hypothetical.

selected.positive: Actual checkpoint contains 1,078,285,824 serialized model parameters (not literal 900M despite '0.9B' product name). Multi-teacher mOPD math/STEM/code training. Publisher AIME 2026 48.5% versus Qwen3.5-2B 38.8%, HumanEval+ 79.9% vs 75.6%; exceptional focused capability under 1.1B.
selected.negative: Publisher-only table; GPQA Diamond 27.3% versus Qwen3.5-2B 54.9%, BFCLv4 28.0 vs 43.6, severe nontransferability to scientific QA/function calling. Custom modeling_k2_horizon.py needs security code review before execution. Name '0.9B' may mislead; use 1.078285824B exact from Appendix.

selected.positive: Base checkpoint is a required learned dependency to use official DSpark 279.5M VLM drafter, separate 3.1235B complete VLM. Preserve target once and refer to it from DSpark without double-download. Japanese among supported languages.
selected.negative: Parent VLM is less novel than DSpark itself; do not score the claimed 3.13x speedup on the target alone. Different from existing LFM3-Omni-2B: LFM2.5 VLM is the exact DSpark-optimized architecture.

selected.positive: 279.5M separately trained draft model conditions on LFM2.5-VL-3B hidden states to enable exact speculative decoding. Official reports H100 decode 2.04–2.66x, end-to-end 1.64–2.27x; M5 Max decode 2.30–3.13x, end-to-end 1.56–2.62x. Preserves genuinely novel high-throughput VLM technique rather than an altered-quality language model.
selected.negative: Full deployed total must count target 3.1235B plus draft 0.2795B = ~3.403B, not 279.5M alone. Not independently reproduced and speedup tested with 16bit model; no demonstrated quantized performance or accuracy improvement. Must pin target-matched backend and versions.

selected.positive: A from-scratch 94.7M code-generating math word problem solver, strong for its extremely small size by symbolic execution: publisher greedy GSM8K test 1319 accuracy 54.7%. System can pair with 94.7M checker and use 48 attempts to reach 72.3%, but paired result is NOT single-model quality.
selected.negative: Not a chatbot; fails unanswerable tasks, irrelevant-number and unit-conversion cases. 48-attempt score is expensive program-execution ensemble and cannot be compared to a single inference. Model-generated Python must never be automatically executed during download or validation.

selected.positive: Companion 94.7M learned verifier evaluates a program result and supports program-candidate weighted voting; this changes the capability of Lilavati beyond one-pass generation. Pair totals 189.4M, still tiny. Separate learned weights are not reproducible from generation model alone.
selected.negative: Verifier only makes sense with precise generator version and a constrained execution sandbox. 72.3% GSM8K at 48 tries from authors, not independent or superior across benchmarks. Never execute arbitrary generated Python from a downloaded model without an audited sandbox.
